bull_bear.body: Strategic investment in EV/tech despite near-term margin dilution; Balance sheet remains net debt-free to fund internal growth; No dividends mentioned specifically but cash flow strong (INR 83.3 Cr).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: EV adoption delayed by 3-5 years; West Asia crisis impacting crude/shipping; Input cost inflation (non-steel); Slow import substitution pace dependent on OEM strategy.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Prudent on accounting (provisions); Realistic on EV timelines (admitting delays); Confident in long-term technology positioning; Transparent about near-term margin headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly shifted EV revenue targets back by 3-5 years, admitting current penetration (4-5% PV, 5-7% 2W) is far below FY26 expectations; The INR 21 Cr loss is a prudent provision with high recovery probability, not an operational cash loss; ARAS entry targets a specific safety gap in Indian 2W market via partnership.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Repeated emphasis on "Strong Cash flow generation and continued Net Debt free Position", with consistent cash generation that "funds group growth and strategic initiatives".
- Management states that "the healthy cash generation from our legacy business continues to support our strategic investments across emerging EV opportunities while maintaining a strong balance sheet".
- Key Ratios slide shows Debt/Equity declining FY22 to FY26 on both series (0.34, 0.31, 0.23, 0.20, 0.17 and 0.31, 0.33, 0.26, 0.28, 0.25) and Networth rising (363.1 to 528.5 Rs cr and 355.8 to 526.3 Rs cr); the extract does not preserve which series is standalone and which is consolidated.
- Net fixed asset turnover over FY22 to FY26 is shown as 1.76, 2.23, 2.30, 2.45, 2.90 on one series and 1.81, 2.70, 3.30, 3.15, 2.38 on the other (same standalone-vs-consolidated ambiguity).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- 2nd largest manufacturer of fasteners for OEMs in India, with pan-India coverage through a network of 100+ distributors
- Fully integrated, in-house manufacturing across every process stage, enabling complete traceability and quality control
- Zero-defect standard: 100% optical sorting on critical product sizes combined with IATF 16949 certification across all facilities
- Continuous product innovation: 80-90 new products introduced annually, backed by a portfolio of 2,000+ part numbers
- SEM is India's leading manufacturer of Motor Control Units, supported by two technology centres and 60+ engineers
- Fasteners business remains strongly cash generative and net debt free, internally funding long-term EV and technology investments
- Early entrant in the HVDC contactor space via technology collaboration with GLVAC YT, China
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Near-term revenue volatility from strategic-customer product in-sourcing — The Company is navigating a transition phase, with near-term performance impacted by product in-sourcing by strategic customers (e.g., a subsidiary's largest customer insourcing motor control unit production).
- Market transition and technology / validation-cycle risk in EV powertrain and power electronics — Expansion into EV powertrain and power electronics segments is characterised by evolving technologies and extended product validation cycles; delays in customer approvals or slower-than-expected adoption may impact revenue realisation and delay revenue ramp-up despite ongoing development and customer interest.
- Supply chain and raw material dependency, including rare earth elements — Dependence on critical components and materials, including electronic components and rare earth elements, may lead to supply disruptions or cost volatility that impacts production planning and cost structures.
- Environmental and regulatory compliance risk — Manufacturing operations are subject to environmental laws and regulations relating to emissions, waste management, energy consumption and workplace safety; tightening standards or non-compliance may increase compliance costs, cause operational disruptions or reputational impact.
- Competitive intensity in fasteners and EV components — Increasing competition from domestic and global players in both the fasteners and EV components businesses may exert pricing pressure and impact margins.
- Cyber security and data privacy risk — Increasing reliance on digital systems and automation exposes the Company to potential cyber threats and data breaches.
- Human resource risk in specialised technology domains — The availability and retention of skilled talent, particularly in specialised areas such as power electronics and advanced manufacturing, remains critical to business growth.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Fasteners: 25-30% domestic market share, entering Tata PV segment; SEM: Transitioning to 4-in-1/5-in-1 integrated units, OBC/DC/DC lines commissioning Q2 FY27; STML: HVDC contactors for import substitution (market est. INR 300 Cr growing to INR 750 Cr).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck claims STL is the "2nd Largest Manufacturer of Automotive Fasteners" and a "Trusted Tier - 1 supplier for manufacturing high-tensile cold-forged fasteners" for 47 years, with segment presence across 2W, 3W, PV, CV, Farm and Off-Highway.
- The group is presented in three parts - Sterling Fasteners (legacy), Sterling E-Mobility (SEM: powertrain and power electronics) and Sterling Tech-Mobility (STML: HVDC contactors and relays) - with stated strategic strengths of "Consistent Market Outperformance", "Double Digit EBITDA Margins", "Net Debt Free", a "Cash-Generative Foundation" and "Premium Product Focus".
- SEM, "formerly known as Sterling Gtake E-Mobility Ltd. (SGEM)", is described as a pioneer and "one of India's leading suppliers of Motor Control Units (MCUs)" that has "evolved into a full-spectrum powertrain and power electronics solutions provider", with regular supplies to more than 20 customers and trials/validation ongoing for 33 customer programs.
- STML is positioned as "First-mover in domestic manufacturing of high-voltage power transmission components" for India's EV and industrial sectors, with strategic alignment to "Make in India" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat".
- Technology access is partnership-led rather than wholly in-house: Jiangsu GTAKE (motor control units), Landworld Technology (DC/DC converters, onboard and offboard chargers), Advanced Electric Machines, UK (rare-earth-magnet-free motors), Kunshan GLVAC Yuantong (HVDC), Minieye and Nanjing Haohang.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group vs standalone divergence] Consolidated total income is shown as 512.6, 774.9, 938.5, 1,038.0, 839.5 Rs cr for FY22-FY26 and consolidated PAT as 25.5, 47.9, 55.4, 58.3, 29.3, while standalone total income is 474.6, 603.5, 613.7, 651.6, 725.9 and standalone PAT 29.7, 41.4, 38.8, 42.9, 64.2 - the consolidated line fell in FY26 while the standalone line rose.
- [New partnerships, 2026] Partnership with China's Minieye Technology Co., Ltd. "to provide ADAS and Driver Monitoring Solutions" and with China's Nanjing Haohang "for ARAS segment for 2Ws" - domains beyond fasteners and powertrain, listed under Active Safety Systems and Electrical Components in the group partnership map.
- [Corporate structure] EV diversification began through 100% subsidiary Sterling Gtake E-Mobility Ltd (SGEM), since renamed Sterling E-Mobility; STML is a wholly owned subsidiary partnered with GLVAC YT (2024) to make advanced high-voltage DC contactors and relays in India.
- [Board] Ten-member board includes Rakesh Batra (Ex-EY Partner and National Leader Auto Sector), Rashmi Urdhwareshe (Ex-Director, ARAI) and Vijay Madhav Paradkar (Ex-VP and Head of M&A, Mahindra & Mahindra).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Sterling Tools operates two complementary businesses: a mature, high-volume fasteners operation that has served as a Tier-1 supplier to India's automotive industry for 47 years, and a fast-growing electric vehicle components business built through its wholly owned subsidiary Sterling E-Mobility Solutions (SEM), India's leading manufacturer of Motor Control Units. The product range spans powertrain, engine, chassis, suspension and seating fasteners for passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, commercial vehicles, farm equipment and construction machinery, alongside MCUs, traction motors, on-board chargers, DC/DC converters and HVDC contactors/relays for electric and hybrid vehicles.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Fasteners (STL, standalone):** High-tensile fasteners for powertrain, engine, chassis, suspension and seating applications
- **EV Powertrain & Power Electronics (SEM):** Motor Control Units (MCUs) for 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, light and heavy commercial vehicles, Integrated motor and controller units (2-in-1, 3-in-1), Multi Function Units (4-in-1, 5-in-1, 6-in-1) for heavy commercial vehicles, On-board chargers and DC/DC converters (including integration with PDUs), Magnet-free traction motors (developed with UK-based Advanced Electric Machines)
- **HVDC (Sterling Tech-Mobility):** High-voltage DC (HVDC) contactors and relays for electric and hybrid electric vehicles
- **Intelligent mobility / safety (technology collaborations):** Advanced Rider Assistance Systems (ARAS) for two-wheelers, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Driver Monitoring Solutions

latest_quarter.body: Steel is pass-through (1-2 month lag); Non-steel costs (energy, chemicals, plastics) seeing extreme inflation causing Q1 FY27 pressure; Mitigation via efficiency gains and customer price hikes expected from Q2 FY27.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Fasteners to outpace industry (>7.9%); Margins: Short-term pressure in Q1 FY27 due to input costs, steady-state target 15%+; Order Inflow: Strong traction in CV electrification; Capex: INR 75 Cr in FY27 for capacity/expansion, commercializing by Q4 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Fasteners: INR 64 Cr new acquisitions in FY26; EV/SEM: 28 active customer programs across 2W, 3W, buses, trucks; STML: Validations ongoing, serial orders expected July/August 2026.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Import substitution in HVDC contactors; Localization of imported fasteners for global OEMs; ARAS (Advanced Rider Assistance Systems) partnership for 2W safety; Integrated powertrain solutions reducing OEM complexity.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- On a consolidated basis, the Company continued to execute its diversification strategy across the fasteners and EV powertrain/power-electronics businesses in FY2025-26, and remains well-positioned for future growth.
- The Company describes a strong track record of rewarding shareholders with substantial dividend payouts, with the final dividend recommendation made in accordance with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy and subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. During the year the Company did not transfer any funds to General Reserve out of profits available for appropriation and did not accept any public deposits.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Sterling Tools has grown its fasteners footprint from a single Faridabad (DLF) plant to three manufacturing plants plus a dedicated wire drawing unit: a wire drawing unit was commissioned in Ballabhgarh (Faridabad, Haryana), a third fasteners plant was set up in Prithla (Palwal, Haryana), and a fourth plant was added in Kolar (Bengaluru, Karnataka). On the EV side, subsidiary Sterling E-Mobility Solutions (SEM) completed a major expansion at its Faridabad site, transforming it into an EV campus with annual MCU capacity of 720,000 units and readiness for product diversification, supported by a second technology centre established in Bengaluru. SEM's product portfolio is expanding beyond MCUs to magnet-free traction motors (developed under a licensing agreement with UK-based Advanced Electric Machines/AEM), on-board chargers and DC/DC converters. Through wholly owned subsidiary Sterling Tech-Mobility Ltd (STML), the Company has partnered with GLVAC YT, China to manufacture high-voltage DC (HVDC) contactors and relays in India, and is commissioning a state-of-the-art HVDC contactor manufacturing facility in Bengaluru as an early entrant in the HVDC space. The Group has also expanded into intelligent mobility and active safety through technology collaboration agreements with Nanjing Haohang (Advanced Rider Assistance Systems for two-wheelers) and MINIEYE (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems and Driver Monitoring Solutions).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The moderation in consolidated revenue and profitability in FY26 was primarily attributable to a shift in the customer mix of a subsidiary following the insourcing of motor control unit production by its largest customer; the Board views this as a temporary variation within an overall growing market and expects the business to recover and grow over the medium term.
- Indian automotive demand is expected to be supported by GST 2.0 reforms and tax relief, lower financing costs from successive RBI repo-rate cuts, recovery in rural demand alongside sustained urban consumption, and rising exports to markets such as the Middle East, Africa and neighbouring countries.
- EV industry growth is expected to be driven by government incentives and localisation push (PM e-DRIVE, FAME-II, PLI schemes), rising EV penetration across two- and three-wheelers (highest growth also seen in passenger three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, LCVs and buses), supply-chain diversification and advanced manufacturing investment, and continued expansion of EV charging infrastructure.
- The domestic manufacturing sector's steady expansion, supported by 'Make in India' and PLI schemes, is expected to continue benefiting the automotive component industry through increasing localisation, supply-chain diversification and growing export opportunities.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Sterling Tools delivered strong FY26 core fastener growth (11.4% revenue, 15.3% EBITDA margin) but flagged a 3-5 year delay in EV adoption timelines, pushing profitability for new EV ventures (SEM, STML) to FY28 while absorbing a one-off bad debt provision in Q4. The company is doubling down on integrated powertrain solutions and safety systems to capture long-term value despite near-term margin headwinds from steel/energy inflation.

risks.risk: Near-term revenue volatility from strategic-customer product in-sourcing
risks.note: The Company is navigating a transition phase, with near-term performance impacted by product in-sourcing by strategic customers (e.g., a subsidiary's largest customer insourcing motor control unit production).

risks.risk: Market transition and technology / validation-cycle risk in EV powertrain and power electronics
risks.note: Expansion into EV powertrain and power electronics segments is characterised by evolving technologies and extended product validation cycles; delays in customer approvals or slower-than-expected adoption may impact revenue realisation and delay revenue ramp-up despite ongoing development and customer interest.

risks.risk: Supply chain and raw material dependency, including rare earth elements
risks.note: Dependence on critical components and materials, including electronic components and rare earth elements, may lead to supply disruptions or cost volatility that impacts production planning and cost structures.

Manufacturing operations are subject to environmental laws and regulations relating to emissions, waste management, energy consumption and workplace safety; tightening standards or non-compliance may increase compliance costs, cause operational disruptions or reputational impact.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity in fasteners and EV components
risks.note: Increasing competition from domestic and global players in both the fasteners and EV components businesses may exert pricing pressure and impact margins.

risks.risk: Cyber security and data privacy risk
risks.note: Increasing reliance on digital systems and automation exposes the Company to potential cyber threats and data breaches.

risks.risk: Human resource risk in specialised technology domains
risks.note: The availability and retention of skilled talent, particularly in specialised areas such as power electronics and advanced manufacturing, remains critical to business growth.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A 47-year Tier-1 auto-component manufacturer combining a mature, cash-generative fasteners business with a fast-growing EV powertrain and power-electronics platform (MCUs, HVDC contactors, ADAS) positioned at the centre of India's mobility transition.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sterling Tools operates two complementary businesses: a mature, high-volume fasteners operation that has served as a Tier-1 supplier to India's automotive industry for 47 years, and a fast-growing electric vehicle components business built through its wholly owned subsidiary Sterling E-Mobility Solutions (SEM), India's leading manufacturer of Motor Control Units. The product range spans powertrain, engine, chassis, suspension and seating fasteners for passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, commercial vehicles, farm equipment and construction machinery, alongside MCUs, traction motors, on-board chargers, DC/DC converters and HVDC contactors/relays for electric and hybrid vehicles.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Sterling E-Mobility Solutions Limited (formerly Sterling Gtake E-Mobility Limited) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; incorporated in Delhi on 10th January 2020; the Company's Material Subsidiary.
- Sterling Tech-Mobility Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary.
- Sterling E-Mobility Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary.
- Sterling Advanced Electric Machines Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary.
- Sterling Overseas Pte Ltd. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (Singapore-registered entity).

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Fasteners: 25-30% domestic market share, entering Tata PV segment; SEM: Transitioning to 4-in-1/5-in-1 integrated units, OBC/DC/DC lines commissioning Q2 FY27; STML: HVDC contactors for import substitution (market est. INR 300 Cr growing to INR 750 Cr).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fasteners (STL, standalone):** High-tensile fasteners for powertrain, engine, chassis, suspension and seating applications
- **EV Powertrain & Power Electronics (SEM):** Motor Control Units (MCUs) for 2-wheelers, 3-wheelers, light and heavy commercial vehicles, Integrated motor and controller units (2-in-1, 3-in-1), Multi Function Units (4-in-1, 5-in-1, 6-in-1) for heavy commercial vehicles, On-board chargers and DC/DC converters (including integration with PDUs), Magnet-free traction motors (developed with UK-based Advanced Electric Machines)
- **HVDC (Sterling Tech-Mobility):** High-voltage DC (HVDC) contactors and relays for electric and hybrid electric vehicles
- **Intelligent mobility / safety (technology collaborations):** Advanced Rider Assistance Systems (ARAS) for two-wheelers, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Driver Monitoring Solutions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Passenger vehicles
- Two-wheelers
- Commercial vehicles
- Farm equipment
- Construction machinery
- Exports to Europe, North America, South America and Asia
- Electric and hybrid vehicle OEMs (2W/3W/LCV/HCV)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Fasteners: INR 64 Cr new acquisitions in FY26; EV/SEM: 28 active customer programs across 2W, 3W, buses, trucks; STML: Validations ongoing, serial orders expected July/August 2026.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Fasteners to outpace industry (>7.9%); Margins: Short-term pressure in Q1 FY27 due to input costs, steady-state target 15%+; Order Inflow: Strong traction in CV electrification; Capex: INR 75 Cr in FY27 for capacity/expansion, commercializing by Q4 FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Import substitution in HVDC contactors; Localization of imported fasteners for global OEMs; ARAS (Advanced Rider Assistance Systems) partnership for 2W safety; Integrated powertrain solutions reducing OEM complexity.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The moderation in consolidated revenue and profitability in FY26 was primarily attributable to a shift in the customer mix of a subsidiary following the insourcing of motor control unit production by its largest customer; the Board views this as a temporary variation within an overall growing market and expects the business to recover and grow over the medium term.
- Indian automotive demand is expected to be supported by GST 2.0 reforms and tax relief, lower financing costs from successive RBI repo-rate cuts, recovery in rural demand alongside sustained urban consumption, and rising exports to markets such as the Middle East, Africa and neighbouring countries.
- EV industry growth is expected to be driven by government incentives and localisation push (PM e-DRIVE, FAME-II, PLI schemes), rising EV penetration across two- and three-wheelers (highest growth also seen in passenger three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, LCVs and buses), supply-chain diversification and advanced manufacturing investment, and continued expansion of EV charging infrastructure.
- The domestic manufacturing sector's steady expansion, supported by 'Make in India' and PLI schemes, is expected to continue benefiting the automotive component industry through increasing localisation, supply-chain diversification and growing export opportunities.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Steel is pass-through (1-2 month lag); Non-steel costs (energy, chemicals, plastics) seeing extreme inflation causing Q1 FY27 pressure; Mitigation via efficiency gains and customer price hikes expected from Q2 FY27.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strategic investment in EV/tech despite near-term margin dilution; Balance sheet remains net debt-free to fund internal growth; No dividends mentioned specifically but cash flow strong (INR 83.3 Cr).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Sterling Tools has grown its fasteners footprint from a single Faridabad (DLF) plant to three manufacturing plants plus a dedicated wire drawing unit: a wire drawing unit was commissioned in Ballabhgarh (Faridabad, Haryana), a third fasteners plant was set up in Prithla (Palwal, Haryana), and a fourth plant was added in Kolar (Bengaluru, Karnataka). On the EV side, subsidiary Sterling E-Mobility Solutions (SEM) completed a major expansion at its Faridabad site, transforming it into an EV campus with annual MCU capacity of 720,000 units and readiness for product diversification, supported by a second technology centre established in Bengaluru. SEM's product portfolio is expanding beyond MCUs to magnet-free traction motors (developed under a licensing agreement with UK-based Advanced Electric Machines/AEM), on-board chargers and DC/DC converters. Through wholly owned subsidiary Sterling Tech-Mobility Ltd (STML), the Company has partnered with GLVAC YT, China to manufacture high-voltage DC (HVDC) contactors and relays in India, and is commissioning a state-of-the-art HVDC contactor manufacturing facility in Bengaluru as an early entrant in the HVDC space. The Group has also expanded into intelligent mobility and active safety through technology collaboration agreements with Nanjing Haohang (Advanced Rider Assistance Systems for two-wheelers) and MINIEYE (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems and Driver Monitoring Solutions).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Prudent on accounting (provisions); Realistic on EV timelines (admitting delays); Confident in long-term technology positioning; Transparent about near-term margin headwinds.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 2nd largest manufacturer of fasteners for OEMs in India, with pan-India coverage through a network of 100+ distributors
- Fully integrated, in-house manufacturing across every process stage, enabling complete traceability and quality control
- Zero-defect standard: 100% optical sorting on critical product sizes combined with IATF 16949 certification across all facilities
- Continuous product innovation: 80-90 new products introduced annually, backed by a portfolio of 2,000+ part numbers
- SEM is India's leading manufacturer of Motor Control Units, supported by two technology centres and 60+ engineers
- Fasteners business remains strongly cash generative and net debt free, internally funding long-term EV and technology investments
- Early entrant in the HVDC contactor space via technology collaboration with GLVAC YT, China

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: EV adoption delayed by 3-5 years; West Asia crisis impacting crude/shipping; Input cost inflation (non-steel); Slow import substitution pace dependent on OEM strategy.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly shifted EV revenue targets back by 3-5 years, admitting current penetration (4-5% PV, 5-7% 2W) is far below FY26 expectations; The INR 21 Cr loss is a prudent provision with high recovery probability, not an operational cash loss; ARAS entry targets a specific safety gap in Indian 2W market via partnership.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group vs standalone divergence] Consolidated total income is shown as 512.6, 774.9, 938.5, 1,038.0, 839.5 Rs cr for FY22-FY26 and consolidated PAT as 25.5, 47.9, 55.4, 58.3, 29.3, while standalone total income is 474.6, 603.5, 613.7, 651.6, 725.9 and standalone PAT 29.7, 41.4, 38.8, 42.9, 64.2 - the consolidated line fell in FY26 while the standalone line rose.
- [New partnerships, 2026] Partnership with China's Minieye Technology Co., Ltd. "to provide ADAS and Driver Monitoring Solutions" and with China's Nanjing Haohang "for ARAS segment for 2Ws" - domains beyond fasteners and powertrain, listed under Active Safety Systems and Electrical Components in the group partnership map.

- [Board] Ten-member board includes Rakesh Batra (Ex-EY Partner and National Leader Auto Sector), Rashmi Urdhwareshe (Ex-Director, ARAI) and Vijay Madhav Paradkar (Ex-VP and Head of M&A, Mahindra & Mahindra).

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
